title: 5 Indian Cult Classics That Flopped At The Box Office
text:
5 Indian Cult Classics That Flopped At The Box Office
Producer: Bhaswati Sengupta
Editor: Aparna Singh | September 24, 2025
Here are 5 interesting facts about the Netflix series.
Jaane Bhi Do Yaaro (1983)
The satire and political commentary did not sit well with the audience initially. Four decades later, it is hailed as a cult masterpiece for its absurdist humour and biting social critique.
Anbe Sivam (2003)
The film explored themes of atheism, communism, and altruism through the story of Nallasivam and Anbarasu. It flopped at the box office. Over time, its philosophical take on unconditional love, portrayed as the essence of God, earned it a cult respect.
Kaagaz Ke Phool (1959)
Guru Dutt’s semi-autobographical classic was rejected by the audiences at the time. Decades later, its influence on Indian filmmakers is undeniable. It is one of cinema’s great cult works.
Mera Naam Joker (1970)
Raj Kapoor’s 4-hour 15 minutes epic, was dismissed by audiences who found the runtime overwhelming. It even pushed RK Studios into financial trouble. After Kapoor died in 1988, its re-release was celebrated with audience recognizing it as ‘ahead of its time.
October (2018)
Shoojit Sircar’s slow pace and realistic treatment of love left audiences underwhelmed. Few years later, it has been admired for its portrayal of the real madness of love.
